pairs: And when king Hezekiah had heard this,
and he covered himself with sackcloth,
and he entered the house of the Lord.
And he sent Eliakim, the first ruler of the house,
and the elders from the priests,
to the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
This day is a day of tribulation,
The sons are ready to be born,
but the woman in labor does not have the strength.

Si forte audiat Dominus Deus tuus universa verba Rabsacis, quem misit rex Assyriorum dominus suus ut exprobraret Deum viventem et argueret verbis, quæ audivit Dominus Deus tuus: et fac orationem pro reliquiis quæ repertæ sunt.

Perhaps the Lord, your God, may hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of the Assyrians, his lord, sent so that he would reproach the living God, and rebuke with words, which the Lord, your God, has heard. And so, offer a prayer on behalf of the remnant that has been found.”
Venerunt ergo servi regis Ezechiæ ad Isaiam.
And the servants of king Hezekiah went to Isaiah.
“So shall you say to your lord.
Noli timere a facie sermonum quos audisti,
Do not be afraid before the face of the words that you have heard,
quibus blasphemaverunt pueri regis Assyriorum me.
by which the servants of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed me.
Behold, I will send a spirit to him,
and he will hear a report,
and he will return to his own land.
et dejiciam eum gladio in terra sua.
And I will bring him down by the sword in his own land.”
et invenit regem Assyriorum expugnantem Lobnam:
and he found the king of the Assyrians fighting against Libnah.
audierat enim quod recessisset de Lachis.
For he had heard that he had withdrawn from Lachish.
Cumque audisset de Tharaca rege Æthiopiæ,
And when he had heard from Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia,
Ecce egressus est ut pugnet adversum te:
he has gone out so that he may fight against you,”
et iret contra eum, misit nuntios ad Ezechiam,
and when he went forth against him, he sent messengers to Hezekiah,
“So shall you say to Hezekiah, the king of Judah:
Non te seducat Deus tuus in quo habes fiduciam,
Let not your God, in whom you trust, lead you astray.
Non tradetur Jerusalem in manus regis Assyriorum.
‘Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.’
Tu enim ipse audisti quæ fecerunt reges Assyriorum universis terris, quomodo vastaverunt eas:
For you yourself have heard what the kings of the Assyrians have done to all the lands, the manner in which they have laid waste to them.
Therefore, how would you alone be able to be freed?
Numquid liberaverunt dii gentium singulos quos vastaverunt patres mei,
Have the gods of the nations freed any of those whom my fathers have destroyed,
et filios Eden qui erant in Thelassar?
and the sons of Eden, who were at Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath,
and the king of the city of Sepharvaim,
Itaque cum accepisset Ezechias litteras de manu nuntiorum,
And so, when Hezekiah had received the letter from the hand of the messengers,
et legisset eas, ascendit in domum Domini,
and had read it, he ascended to the house of the Lord,
and he spread it out before the Lord.
And he prayed in his sight,
tu es Deus solus regum omnium terræ:
you alone are God, over all the kings of the earth.
et vide: audi omnia verba Sennacherib,
And hear all the words of Sennacherib,
qui misit ut exprobraret nobis Deum viventem.
who sent so that he might reproach the living God before us.
the kings of the Assyrians have devastated all peoples
Et miserunt deos eorum in ignem:
And they have cast their gods into the fire.
but instead were the works of men’s hands,
Now therefore, O Lord our God,
salvos nos fac de manu ejus,
bring us salvation from his hand,
ut sciant omnia regna terræ quia tu es Dominus Deus solus.
so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the Lord God.”
Misit autem Isaias filius Amos ad Ezechiam,
Then Isaiah, the son of Amoz, sent to Hezekiah,
“Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel:
Quæ deprecatus es me super Sennacherib rege Assyriorum,
I have heard what you beseeched from me, concerning Sennacherib,
Iste est sermo, quem locutus est Dominus de eo:
This is the word that the Lord has spoken about him:
Sprevit te, et subsannavit te, virgo filia Sion:
The virgin daughter of Zion has spurned and ridiculed you.
post tergum tuum caput movit, filia Jerusalem.
The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head behind your back.
Against whom have you exalted your voice,
et elevasti in excelsum oculos tuos?
and lifted up your eyes on high?
Against the Holy One of Israel!
Per manum servorum tuorum exprobrasti Domino,
By the hand of your servants, you have reproached the Lord,
In multitudine curruum meorum ascendi excelsa montium in summitate Libani,
‘By the multitude of my chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the summit of Lebanon.
And I have cut down its sublime cedars,
Et ingressus sum usque ad terminos ejus,
And I have entered even to its limits.
et siccavi vestigiis pedum meorum omnes aquas clausas.
and I dried up all the enclosed waters with the steps of my feet.’
Numquid non audisti quid ab initio fecerim?
But have you not heard what I have done from the beginning?
From the days of antiquity, I have formed it,
et nunc adduxi: eruntque in ruinam collium pugnantium civitates munitæ.
and now I have brought it to be. And fortified cities of fighting men will become piles of ruins.
And whoever may settle in these,
They have become like the hay of the field,
and like weeds sprouting on the rooftops,
quæ arefacta est antequam veniret ad maturitatem.
which dry up before they reached maturity.
and your way, I knew beforehand,
along with your fury against me.
Insanisti in me, et superbia tua ascendit in aures meas:
You have been maddened against me, and your arrogance has ascended to my ears.
ponam itaque circulum in naribus tuis,
And so, I will place a ring in your nose,
and a bit between your lips.
et reducam te in viam per quam venisti.
And I will lead you back along the way by which you came.
Eat this year whatever you will find,
whatever may spring up of itself.
Et quodcumque reliquum fuerit de domo Juda,
And whatever will have been left behind, from the house of Judah,
Indeed, a remnant shall go forth from Jerusalem,
et quod salvetur de monte Sion:
and what may be saved shall go forth from mount Zion.
The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall accomplish this.
Quam ob rem hæc dicit Dominus de rege Assyriorum:
For this reason, thus says the Lord about the king of the Assyrians:
He shall not enter into this city,
nor shoot an arrow into it,
nor overtake it with the shield,
By the way that he came,
And he shall not enter this city,
And I will protect this city,
and I will save it for my own sake,
and for the sake of my servant David.”
Factum est igitur in nocte illa,
And so it happened that, in the same night,
an Angel of the Lord went and struck down,
et percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia.
in the camp of the Assyrians, one hundred and eighty-five thousand.
And when he had risen up, at first light,
he saw all the bodies of the dead.
et reversus est Sennacherib rex Assyriorum,
And Sennacherib, the king of the Assyrians,
Cumque adoraret in templo Nesroch deum suum,
And while he was worshipping in the temple of his god, Nisroch,
Adramelech et Sarasar filii ejus percusserunt eum gladio,
his sons, Adram-melech and Sharezer, struck him with the sword.
And they fled into the land of the Armenians.
et regnavit Asarhaddon filius ejus pro eo.
And Esarhaddon, his son, reigned in his place.
